label: copy-phase fed-back "a" in the middle of the copy (recall_idx >= 3, not near the end)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost always when the fed-back input is the letter a (93% of activation mass has in_tok = a; t, w and the digit 2 make up most of the rest, at low magnitude). It never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter, and never on a copied a at recall_idx < 3. It is strongest when a was original token 2-3, so the output is recall_idx 3-4 (t = 12-13). It is weaker or silent when only 0-1 outputs remain. The top activations (up to 3.3) are a followed by t or 2 in long sequences (L = 8-9); out_tok being t, 2, y or k raises the firing rate, while vowels and some letters (e, l, h, x) as the next output often mean no firing. Repeated a in the original sequence gives weak activations. Precision is limited because many copy-phase a inputs that meet the predicate stay silent, and the token-identity dependence on out_tok has no clean description. Simpler alternative (phase 2, in_tok a, recall_idx >= 3): dev P 0.35, R 0.87, mass recall 0.93.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: a, t, 2, w, k, c; least: 3, 1, l, x) and the token being output (most: t, 2, k, y, w, c; least: h, b, -, f); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=4, recall_idx=3, L=9 & t=13.
